questions.q: In "Cloud models and shared responsibility Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Sort each workload into move as is, adjust slightly, rebuild, replace with ready software, or retire, and give a one-line reason for each choice.
Send two user notices: one week and one day before.
Mark what must run together.
Write down which cloud services you already use without knowing, such as free email or file sharing.

questions.q: In "Inventory and dependencies Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Schedule a six-month check for unused resources and security settings.
Models: infrastructure (rented machines), platform (managed tools) and software (ready-made apps), each sold as a service.
List every application, its owner, its data size in gigabytes, its users and the other systems it calls; aim for one row per item in a simple sheet.
Run a pilot with a low-risk system first, such as shared files.

questions.q: In "Choose the approach Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: List servers, apps, data size, users, licences and links to other systems.
Compare on cost, time, risk and skill needed.
List every application, its owner, its data size in gigabytes, its users and the other systems it calls; aim for one row per item in a simple sheet.

questions.q: In "Cost model Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Update the inventory and costs.
Include staff time for the move and for training.
Record skills needed and who will learn them.
Compare speed, cost, complaints and downtime with goals.

questions.q: In "Security and data Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Hand over a runbook with accounts, backups, alerts and contacts, and run a short walk-through so the owner can do each task without you.
Note the exit route: how you would leave a provider if prices rise.
Turn on multi-step sign-in for every admin account on day one and use separate accounts for daily work and for administration.
Estimate monthly cost as machine hours, storage in gigabytes, data transfer out and support, and compare with your current yearly cost divided by twelve.

questions.q: In "Test, back up and rehearse Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Compare on cost, time, risk and skill needed.
Mark what must run together.
Write the cut-over steps minute by minute.
Check the provider's location for data and the law that applies.

questions.q: In "Cut-over and rollback Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Compare after 30 days against the baseline for speed, uptime, cost and user complaints, and present the four numbers on one page.
Count compute, storage, data out, support and backups.
Rehost (as-is) is quick; replatform (small change) saves more; rebuild costs most.
Define rollback triggers in numbers, for example error rate above 2 percent or login failures over 10, and keep the old system untouched until day seven.

questions.q: In "Measure and hand over Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Compare after 30 days against the baseline for speed, uptime, cost and user complaints, and present the four numbers on one page.
Public, private and mixed (hybrid) clouds.
